name: Platypus MasterPlatypusV4 emergencyWithdraw solvency check
summary: MasterPlatypusV4.emergencyWithdraw() checked solvency before zeroing the user's staked LP balance. The check therefore saw the collateral still present and passed, after which the function returned that collateral without requiring repayment of the USP debt it secured.

loss.notes: Platypus reports $9.19 million lost across three attacks by the same exploiter and defect. The anchored first attack accounted for approximately $8.5 million; the reported gross campaign amount precedes subsequent freezes and recoveries.

ageReset.description: The proxy's Upgraded event selected the MasterPlatypusV4 implementation containing the vulnerable emergencyWithdraw ordering; no later Upgraded event occurred before the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the live Avalanche receipt and call trace, proxy creation trace, every proxy Upgraded event from deployment through the exploit, the implementation slot and pre-exploit runtime hash, the reproduction source, Omniscia's technical post-mortem, and Platypus's campaign report. The attack contract calls emergencyWithdraw(4) on proxy 0xff6934aac9c94e1c39358d4fdcf70aeca77d0ab0, which delegatecalls implementation 0xc007f27b757a782c833c568f5851ae1dfe0e6ec7. The implementation checks PlatypusTreasure.isSolvent while the user's LP amount still backs the debt, then transfers the LP and only afterwards zeros the amount. The proxy emitted one pre-exploit Upgraded event, at 22409704:4:3, selecting the traced implementation; no later event occurred before the exploit and its runtime hash matches the declaration. Platypus reports a $9.19 million gross campaign across three attacks by the same exploiter and bug, of which the anchored first attack was approximately $8.5 million.

limitations: The loss is Platypus's rounded gross campaign estimate; the three-attack asset basket is not independently repriced here.
